$comment: DR-5 / G1 policy data for servers/exarchos-mcp/scripts/cli-derivation-guard.ts —
command names tolerated as hand-written string literals in the CLI composition root
servers/exarchos-mcp/src/adapters/cli/cli.ts, each with an OWNER and an ENFORCED expiry.
Every file named in this comment must be a repo-relative path that EXISTS: the guard
refuses to read this policy otherwise. (An earlier revision pointed at a
cli-derivation-seam module that had been renamed away, so the pointer a future author
follows led nowhere. The reference is bound now rather than merely corrected.)
The composition root carries 14 `.command(` sites: 3 derivation loops (cliName,
harness, commandName) and 11 hand-written literals. TEN of those eleven are tracked
here. The eleventh is merge-orchestrate, which is the KILL FIXTURE and is not
allowlistable at all (see below). The numbers above are stated for a reader; nothing
reads them — the guard derives its population from the parse on every run, and
`auditCliAllowlistMembership` fails BOTH ways: a literal that is not tracked here, and
an entry here that names no live literal. There is no way to park a paid-down entry.
── HOW THIS LIST SHRINKS, AND HOW IT CANNOT GROW ───────────────────────────
Register the verb through a derivation helper (registerActionCommand, the composite-tool
loop, or the harness loop) so its name comes from a registry declaration, then MOVE its
line from `allowed` to `retired`, swapping `expires` for `retiredAt: '<the date you paid
it down>'`. That is the only supported edit.
Entries are never ADDED to either map. The seed key set is `allowed` UNION `retired`, and
that union is INVARIANT under the move above — so the frozen digest in
servers/exarchos-mcp/scripts/cli-derivation-seed-pin.ts never changes for legal work, and
any change to it is by construction someone widening what the seed covers. This is what
makes an IN-PLACE SWAP (drop one, add another, count unchanged) a red build rather than a
diff a reviewer has to notice.
── THE EXPIRY IS ENFORCED, NOT ADVISORY ────────────────────────────────────
`expires` is read by `auditCliDerivationExpiry`, and an entry past its date FAILS. An
entry may not name a date later than the single pinned horizon in
servers/exarchos-mcp/scripts/cli-derivation-seed-pin.ts, so per-entry renewal is
impossible and re-dating the whole debt is one conspicuous line in a file of frozen
values. The clock is read ONCE, at the gate entrypoint
servers/exarchos-mcp/scripts/cli-derivation-ratchet-guard.ts — never inside a unit test,
because a deadline must redden the MERGE and not a developer's local run.
The list reaches ZERO at DR-19. Zero is not a state this file holds: an allowlist that
resolves zero entries FAILS (that is what a moved or renamed policy file looks like), so
the last paydown DELETES this file, the pin, and the expiry audit in one commit.
── KILL FIXTURE — DO NOT ADD 'merge-orchestrate' HERE ──────────────────────
It is the guard's live failing subject: merge_orchestrate is declared BOTH as a registry
action (with posture: 'shared-mutating') and by hand in
servers/exarchos-mcp/src/adapters/cli/cli.ts. An earlier revision of this policy allowlisted
it, which neutralized the exact rejection DR-5 requires. The guard REFUSES to read this
file at all if the name appears in EITHER map (see KILL_FIXTURE_COMMANDS in
servers/exarchos-mcp/scripts/cli-derivation-guard.ts). The remedy is to delete the
hand-written .command('merge-orchestrate') call, never to exempt it.
The owner is the subsystem that owns the verb's remediation, taken from what the
hand-written command actually promotes: 'orchestration' and 'workflow-platform' name the
composite tool the command dispatches through (the same owner vocabulary the DR-4 and
DR-2 waiver ledgers use); 'event-store' owns the emission catalog; 'cli-surface' covers
the verbs with no composite tool behind them at all — introspection, the MCP server-mode
verb, the version verb, and the two one-release rename stubs removed at v3.0.
